newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS seen launching Swiss Internet banking.
newsitem.headline: CS seen launching Swiss Internet banking.

text.p: Credit Suisse is about to become the first of Switzerland's three big global banks to launch retail banking services on the worldwide internet computer network, Swiss newspapers reported.
The Sunday paper SonntagsZeitung and the business bi-weekly Finanz und Wirtschaft said the launch of internet banking would be the subject of a Credit Suisse news conference on Thursday, April 10.
Credit Suisse, the Swiss banking arm of the Credit Suisse Group that also includes CS First Boston, called the news conference unexpectedly on Friday after bourse closing.
The bank would say only that the event concerned "a new, attractive product in the area of direct banking."
Credit Suisse Group spokeswoman Karin Rhomberg declined to elaborate or to comment on the newspaper reports about an Internet launch when contacted by Reuters.
The weekly Sonntagszeitung said the Internet service would allow customers to take care of such matters as checking on account balances, paying bills or buying and selling stocks.

"Apparently, it (Credit Suisse) is the first Swiss bank to master the technical problems releated to security and the compatability of the complex data processing elements," the SonntagsZeitung wrote.
It said Credit Suisse would use an encryption and decoding software called SecureNet to protect data flowing between customers and the bank from being read by outsiders.
SecureNet was developed by a Swiss company, r3security engineering ag, the newspaper said.
"The technological breakthrough by the Credit Suisse Group has an effect on the entire Swiss business world," the paper said.

By finding a secure enough program to protect financial data on the public Internet, Credit Suisse was effectively opening the Internet to other lucrative commercial uses that have been stalled so far by worries about the safety of money and information, SonntagsZeitung said.
Retail bank services are already available electronically for customers at Credit Suisse and most other Swiss banks, but they use an older technology hooked into the cable television network.

SontagsZeitungs aid the advantages of the Internet would be that customers could use the same familiar computer network and technology for viewing and making changes in their accounts. In the mid-term, the Internet should also prove faster than the existing videotext system.
By estimates, the Internet has more than 200,000 users in Switzerland out of a total population of about seven million people. ((-- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340))
